title: Flow Cytometry Assay for Cytolytic Activity of Mouse MAIT and NK Cells
author: Sugimoto, Fujita, et al.
materials: Vybrant CFDA SE cell tracer kit

steps.title: Prepare media, reagents and gelatin plates
steps.instruction: Prepare all culture media, cytokines and reagents as listed in the Materials and Equipment section, then coat plates with gelatin.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the culture media, cytokines and reagents as described in the Materials and Equipment section.
Add 1 mL of 0.1 % gelatin to each well of a 12‑well plate and 6 mL of 0.1 % gelatin to each 10‑cm dish (gelatin stored at 20‑25 °C, usable up to 3 months).
Incubate the coated plates and dishes at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for at least 30 min to allow gelatin coating.
Store the coated plates/dishes in the incubator for up to ~10 days; do not let the gelatin dry completely.

steps.title: Prepare and maintain OP9/DLL1 stromal cells
steps.instruction: Thaw, culture, and regularly passage OP9/DLL1 cells to keep a near‑confluent monolayer.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm 10 mL OP9 medium (stored at 4 °C ≤1 month) in a 15‑mL conical tube in a 37 °C water bath.
Quick‑thaw frozen OP9/DLL1 cells at 37 °C and transfer them to the pre‑warmed OP9 medium.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL OP9 medium.
Plate 1.0–1.2 × 10⁶ cells in a 10‑cm culture dish; spread evenly by gentle shaking.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until the culture is nearly confluent.
Passage the confluent monolayer:
i. Remove medium and wash the monolayer twice with 5 mL PBS (20‑25 °C).
ii. Add 0.5 mL of 0.25 % Trypsin‑1 mM EDTA (stored at 4 °C ≤2 weeks; use at 20‑25 °C) and spread.
iii. Incubate 3–5 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
iv. Add 4 mL OP9 medium and pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
v. Transfer the suspension to a 15‑mL tube and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
vi. Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in an appropriate volume of OP9 medium.
vii. Plate cells at a 1:3 to 1:8 split ratio so that the same confluency is reached every 3 days.
viii. Return dishes to the incubator.
Repeat the passage steps as needed to maintain the OP9/DLL1 culture.

steps.title: Prepare co‑culture plates for reMAIT differentiation
steps.instruction: Seed freshly trypsinized OP9/DLL1 cells onto gelatinized 10‑cm dishes and culture for 4–6 days.

substeps.instruction: Trypsinize a near‑confluent OP9/DLL1 monolayer and obtain a single‑cell suspension as described in the passage steps above.
Remove gelatinized 10‑cm dishes from the incubator and aspirate off the residual gelatin solution.
Plate the OP9/DLL1 suspension into the gelatinized dishes using the same passage ratio as the maintenance culture, adding OP9 medium.
Incubate for 4–6 days, replacing half of the OP9 medium every other day.

steps.title: Prepare mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) feeder cells
steps.instruction: Thaw, plate, and culture mitomycin‑C‑treated MEFs on gelatinized 12‑well plates.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm 10 mL MEF medium in a 15‑mL conical tube at 37 °C.
Quick‑thaw a frozen vial containing 1.25 × 10⁶ mitomycin‑C‑treated MEFs at 37 °C and transfer to the pre‑warmed MEF medium.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 12 mL MEF medium (stored at 4 °C ≤1 month).
Remove a gelatinized 12‑well plate from the incubator and aspirate the gelatin solution.
Add 1 mL of the MEF suspension to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 days.

steps.title: Prepare and maintain mouse MAIT‑iPSCs
steps.instruction: Thaw iPSCs, culture on MEF feeders, and passage when 70–80 % confluent.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm 10 mL MEF medium in a 15‑mL tube at 37 °C.
Quick‑thaw a frozen vial of mouse MAIT‑iPSCs at 37 °C and transfer to the pre‑warmed MEF medium.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL mES medium (stored at 4 °C ≤2 weeks).
Aspirate medium from a well containing MEF feeder cells prepared in the previous step.
Seed the iPSC suspension onto the MEF feeder well.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until iPSCs reach 70–80 % confluency; change half of the medium daily with fresh mES medium.
When 70–80 % confluent, passage the iPSCs:
i. Wash cells twice with 1 mL PBS.
ii. Add 200 µL of 0.25 % Trypsin‑1 mM EDTA per well and incubate 2–3 min at 37 °C.
iii. Verify complete detachment, then add 1 mL MEF medium and pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
iv. Count cells; use 1.2 × 10⁵ cells for a 3‑day passage or 6 × 10⁴ cells for a 4‑day passage.
v. Remove medium from a fresh MEF‑feeder well and add 1 mL mES medium.
vi. Seed the appropriate number of iPSCs onto the feeder.
vii. Incubate until 70–80 % confluency, changing half of the medium daily with mES medium.

steps.title: Isolate mouse NK cells from C57BL/6 spleen
steps.instruction: Harvest spleens, enrich lymphocytes by Percoll gradient, and purify NK cells by negative magnetic selection.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize three 8‑ to 12‑week‑old C57BL/6 mice and remove their spleens.
Place a 40 µm cell strainer in a 10‑cm petri dish and position the spleens on the strainer.
Add 3–4 mL cR10 medium and mash the spleens with the plunger of a 2.5‑mL syringe to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Transfer the suspension to a 15‑mL tube; rinse the dish with an additional 5 mL cR10 and combine the washes.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 4 min and discard the supernatant.
Add 3 mL 67 % Percoll (stored at 4 °C ≤3 months) to a new 15‑mL tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 8 mL 40 % Percoll (stored at 4 °C ≤3 months).
Using low dispense speed, slowly layer the 40 % Percoll suspension onto the 67 % Percoll while tilting the tube ≈30° so the suspension flows down the inner wall, forming a clear interface.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 20 min at 20–25 °C with the brake off.
Collect the white interphase layer (boundary of the two Percoll layers) into a new 15‑mL tube.
Fill the tube with PBS, invert several times to mix.
Centrifuge at 700 × g for 7 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL MACS buffer (stored at 4 °C ≤3 months).
Filter the suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer.
Count cells (typically 3–5 × 10⁷ cells from three spleens).
Adjust cell concentration to 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL with MACS buffer.
Add 2 µL biotin antibody cocktail per 1 × 10⁷ cells; incubate on ice for 15 min. (Critical: exact volume required for purity.)
Add 5 mL MACS buffer and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in MACS buffer at 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL.
Add 2 µL streptavidin nanobeads per 1 × 10⁷ cells; incubate on ice for 15 min.
Add 5 mL MACS buffer and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL MACS buffer.
Perform negative selection using an LS column:
i. Place the LS column in a magnetic separator and equilibrate with 3 mL MACS buffer.
ii. Position an empty 15‑mL conical tube beneath the column to collect the flow‑through (negative fraction).
iii. Apply the cell suspension onto the column through a 40 µm strainer; collect the flow‑through.
iv. Wash the column twice with 3 mL MACS buffer each time, collecting the washes in the same tube.
Centrifuge the collected negative fraction at 400 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 3 mL cR10 medium.
Count the purified NK cells (expected 1.5–5 × 10⁶ NK cells; purity ≈50–60 %).
Take 1 × 10⁴ cells for a purity check:
i. Add 0.5 µL FITC‑NK1.1, 0.5 µL PE‑CD49b, and 50 µL FACS buffer (total 50 µL) per 5 × 10⁴ cells.
ii. Incubate 20 min at 20–25 °C in the dark.
iii. Wash with FACS buffer, resuspend in FACS buffer containing 7‑AAD.
iv. Acquire data on a flow cytometer.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps in a cytolytic assay for redifferentiated mouse MAIT-like cells from iPS Cells (iPSCs) (reMAIT cells). While human MAIT cells comprise about 0.5%–10% of peripheral blood T cells, less than 0.05% represent MAIT cells in laboratory mice. To investigate the function of MAIT cells in mouse disease models, we obtain a large amount of reMAIT cells from iPSCs. For this purpose, the iPSCs must possess rearranged T cell receptor (TCR) loci specific for MAIT cells. Therefore, the iPSCs must be established from MAIT cells. Another way to obtain mouse MAIT cells is to isolate them from the tissues of laboratory mice with increased number of MAIT cells. Such mice may include MAIT-TCR transgenic mice,2 B6-Cast mice,3 wild-type mice exposed to the vaccine strains of bacteria or MAIT cell ligands such as vitamin B2 metabolites,4 and Vα19 or Vβ8 mice generated via chimeric mice from MAIT-iPSC, which we recently reported.5,6 When using MR1-tetramers that specifically detect MAIT cells, it should be recalled that MAIT cells are activated during the purification process.1 Therefore, when interpreting results using MAIT cells purified with the MR1 tetramer, one must be cautious about whether the in vitro results truly reflect the in vivo features.
